# Autonomy — Long Runs, Aborts & Handoff

_Applies when: running long, autonomous, or multi-session work (overnight runs, watchdog crons, resumable workflows). The principles hold on any target; the named mechanics (`SendMessage`, `TaskList`/`TaskOutput`, `Workflow`, crons) are Claude-harness features._

## An aborted agent is not an empty agent

- **On abort, resume the agent** — the abort message carries the `agentId` + the literal `SendMessage`
  syntax to continue it; its context is intact and builds on half-finished work, a restart rediscovers all.
- **Never silently replace an aborted agent's work with your own** — you already hold its agentId, and
  you lose findings you cannot know it had. Verified: a parent wrote off two `ENOTFOUND`-aborted
  subagents, redid their review and caught only **1 of 3 majors**; one of the two, third-party-resumed
  7 min later, delivered 3 major + 8 minor, incl. a remount tearing down the realtime master subscriber.
- Harness caveat: a resumed agent's result is routed to **whoever resumed it**, not to the original
  `parentAgentId`. A third-party resume silently re-parents the result.

## The living status log — it IS the handoff point

**The transcript is not a persistence layer.** Agents **write findings to a file**, not only into a
returned message — no abort can destroy them and any party can read them. One log survived two
reboots and several session deaths; the chat did not. Update after every significant step. Sections:

- decisions made by the human · decisions made autonomously (time / decision / rationale)
- running task IDs (for `TaskOutput`) · next steps in order · hard breakpoints
- open cross-repo follow-ups · literal resume commands (e.g. `Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId})`)
- **session ownership** (mandatory): session id · repo/slice held · since when · what another session must NOT touch

## Two sessions are two agents — reconcile before you commit

Sessions cannot see each other; the living log is their only shared state. Verified: two parallel
sessions built wave 1 TWICE, divergently — caught only by a manual `git log` diff. Same disease as
`25-orchestration`'s "consolidate shared semantics", one level up: not two agents, two SESSIONS.

- **Before every commit/push: `git fetch`, then diff `HEAD` against the branch's OWN upstream AND
  `origin/<default-branch>`.** Upstream commits are a push conflict, a moved default branch only a
  moved base ⇒ RECONCILE first. `origin-divergence-check` reports the counts, never blocks (ADR-0025).

## The watchdog cron

A **durable, recurring** cron: (a) reads the living log + plan; (b) checks running work non-blocking
(`TaskList`/`TaskOutput`), restarting dead workflows via `Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId})`, dead
agents from the log's brief; (c) starts the log's next step if idle; (d) **stops at hard breakpoints**,
never crossing one without human go-ahead (publishes, DB migrations, auto-deploy pushes, final
acceptance); (e) makes recommended-decisions autonomously, writing **each** to the log; (f) deletes its cron.

## Worktree-per-session — the default for code-writing sessions

- **Every code-writing session runs in its own git worktree** in the sibling directory
  `<repo>-worktrees/<slug>` — never in-repo. This **reverses** the old "worktrees are the exception"
  stance (**ADR-0030**): isolation is the default now. Read-only / purely conversational sessions
  skip it — no `pnpm install` overhead for a trivial question.
- **Untracked or generated state does not travel** — neither the GENERATED `CLAUDE.md` +
  `.claude/rules/*` (**ADR-0015**) nor `.gitnexus/` comes with `git worktree add`, and nothing errors.
  `worktree-bootstrap.sh` auto-restores the config; the graph owes a declared substitute (`skill:gitnexus-guide`).
- `.git` is a **file** in a worktree, so any literal `.git/<x>` path fails — use `"$(git rev-parse --git-dir)/<x>"`;
  worktree detection = `--git-dir` differs from `--git-common-dir`.
- Teardown cannot complete autonomously: `git worktree remove` fails on `node_modules` ("Directory
  not empty") and `rm -rf` is correctly denied by the permission system — leftover dirs need a human.
- Agents in **different repos need no shared worktree** among themselves — the per-session worktree
  isolates THIS session's work in ITS repo; it does not multiply worktrees across repos.
